issues.description: signing_mode_enum has non-exhaustive branches with a silent fall-through default
issues.detail: The (is_hex, safe_mode) mapping uses if/elif with three explicit branches and an implicit CHIP_0002 default for the fourth case. A reader must truth-table to verify completeness. Make it total via an explicit match or full if/elif/else so the mapping is provable from inspection.

issues.description: sign_message and verify_signature duplicate the mode-to-bytes dispatch
issues.detail: Both functions reimplement the SigningMode -> message-bytes mapping. This invites drift: a future CHIP mode added to one branch would silently disagree with the other. Extract a single _message_to_bytes(mode, message) helper and call it from both sides so 'verify reverses sign' is textual rather than coincidental.

issues.description: verify_signature docstring is stale boilerplate referencing a nonexistent 'request' parameter
issues.detail: The function was lifted from the RPC handler verbatim, including ':param request:', but now takes keyword-only fields (signing_mode, public_key, message, signature, address). Rewrite the docstring to state the actual inputs, outputs, and the address-binding invariant, or delete it. Stale docs in a freshly extracted library function are worse than none.

issues.description: verify_signature leaks the RPC response type VerifySignatureResponse into the util layer
issues.detail: chia/wallet/util/signing.py imports VerifySignatureResponse from wallet_request_types and returns it directly. The signing utility's contract should be a plain bool plus an error reason, not an RPC-shaped DTO. As written the util is coupled to the RPC schema's evolution and cannot be reused without dragging it along.

issues.description: convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is an instance method that uses no instance state
issues.detail: Wallet.convert_secret_key_to_synthetic only forwards to calculate_synthetic_secret_key with a module-level constant. Callers reach through main_wallet to derive keys for unrelated DID/NFT wallets, conflating pure derivation with wallet state. Move it to chia/wallet/util/signing.py as a free function (or make it staticmethod) so the boundary is clean.

issues.description: test_sign_message_by_address does not assert isValid on the verify response
issues.detail: The new test calls verify_signature but never asserts the returned VerifySignatureResponse.isValid is True. A regression that makes every signature fail verification would still let this test pass. Bind the result and assert response.isValid is True so the postcondition is actually checked.

synthesis.summary: The panel agrees this is a sensible mechanical extraction of sign_message and verify_signature into chia/wallet/util/signing.py with the algorithmic content preserved, but the cleanup stops one step short. The new util module duplicates the SigningMode-to-bytes dispatch between sign and verify, ships a non-exhaustive signing_mode_enum with a silent fall-through, and carries a stale ':param request:' docstring. It also leaks the RPC response type into the util layer, and convert_secret_key_to_synthetic is misplaced on the base Wallet. Small, fixable changes — then land it.
